notes: Every semantic change within the declared change-management sentence scope was reviewed against the extracted text of both PDFs.

old.start_quote: In general, a bank’s operational risk exposure is increased when a bank engages in new activities or develops new products; enters unfamiliar markets; implements new business processes or technology systems; and/or engages in businesses that are geographically distant from the head office.
old.end_quote: In general, a bank’s operational risk exposure is increased when a bank engages in new activities or develops new products; enters unfamiliar markets; implements new business processes or technology systems; and/or engages in businesses that are geographically distant from the head office.

new.start_quote: In general, a bank’s operational risk exposure evolves when a bank initiates change, such as engaging in new activities or developing new products or services; entering into unfamiliar markets or jurisdictions; implementing new or modifying business processes or technology systems; and/or engaging in businesses that are geographically distant from the head office.
new.end_quote: In general, a bank’s operational risk exposure evolves when a bank initiates change, such as engaging in new activities or developing new products or services; entering into unfamiliar markets or jurisdictions; implementing new or modifying business processes or technology systems; and/or engaging in businesses that are geographically distant from the head office.

changes.old_quote: In general, a bank’s operational risk exposure is increased when a bank engages in new activities or develops new products; enters unfamiliar markets; implements new business processes or technology systems; and/or engages in businesses that are geographically distant from the head office.
changes.new_quote: In general, a bank’s operational risk exposure evolves when a bank initiates change, such as engaging in new activities or developing new products or services; entering into unfamiliar markets or jurisdictions; implementing new or modifying business processes or technology systems; and/or engaging in businesses that are geographically distant from the head office.
changes.note: The revised principle broadens new-product approval into lifecycle-oriented change management.
